findings.reason: the same count/enumeration mismatch that earlier reviews sent back on §47 and §50 leaves a reviewer unable to tell which cases the gate was meant to cover, and the seven-day removal rule in the deliverable would then have no case proving it.
findings.text: §53's done-when reads "a test with four directories finds, after one prune pass, the dead local host's directory removed and the other three kept: a live local host, a host on another node whose pid is absent here, and a node-less directory touched within seven days", then adds "A node-less directory older than seven days is removed", which is a fifth directory and a second removal, so the gate's scope is self-contradictory — a builder can implement four directories with one removal and close the section while the seven-day-old node-less case is never exercised

findings.reason: §52's done-when (c) requires §51's two-session case to still draw one grant and one end and requires "test files importing reckon/crew_follow_commands.py ... show no added failure against base", so the node cannot satisfy its own gate without editing a file it is not granted, and the builder will either breach scope or leave the suite red.
findings.text: §52 decides "hosted" from RECKON_SESSION_HOST_SETTLE, but §51's merged test (tests/test_a_pane_draws_a_lift_once_per_host.py:83-99, and its fixture docstring) simulates a hosted follower by setting only RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER and never RECKON_SESSION_HOST_SETTLE, so after §52's change test_a_host_following_two_sessions_draws_one_grant_and_one_end and test_the_claim_is_keyed_on_the_host_when_one_is_present both fail, yet §52's declared write paths are "reckon/crew_follow_commands.py and tests/test_a_lift_claim_key_names_a_real_host.py" — the file that must change is out of scope
